hook.explorer: Make a tiny light turn on!
hook.builder: Build your very first circuit and light up an LED.
hook.engineer: Build a series LED circuit and work out why the resistor has to be there.

instruction.explorer: Put the red wire in the red hole at the top.
instruction.builder: Connect the battery's red wire to the top red rail, then run a jumper from the rail down to hole A5.
instruction.engineer: Tie the 9V positive to the upper + bus, then jumper the bus to row 5 (A5).

expect.builder: Nothing lights up yet - the loop isn't finished.
expect.engineer: Open circuit so far. No current flows until the loop closes.

instruction.explorer: Put the stripey brake in. It goes in two holes.
instruction.builder: Push the 330Ω resistor into E5 and E10. It doesn't matter which way round it goes.
instruction.engineer: Place the 330Ω limiting resistor between row 5 and row 10. Resistors have no polarity.

explanation.explorer: The brake stops the light getting too much zap.
explanation.builder: Without the brake, the light gets far too much electricity all at once and burns out - in about a second.
explanation.engineer: The LED has no internal current limit. Its Vf pins at about 2V, so the resistor sets the current: (9 - 2) / 330 = 21mA.

instruction.explorer: Put the light in. The LONG leg goes on top.
instruction.builder: Push the LED's long leg into A10 and its short leg into A15. The long leg must be the one nearer the battery - LEDs only work one way round.
instruction.engineer: LED anode (long leg) to row 10, cathode (short leg, flat side) to row 15. Reversed, it simply won't conduct.

expect.explorer: Still nothing! One more wire to go.
expect.builder: Still dark - the electricity has nowhere to go home to yet.
expect.engineer: Still open. The cathode has no return path to the negative terminal.

instruction.explorer: Last wire! Now it lights up!
instruction.builder: Run the last jumper from E15 to the black rail at the top. That completes the loop.
instruction.engineer: Jumper row 15 to the negative bus to close the loop.

expect.builder: The LED should be glowing now. If not, try turning the LED around.
expect.engineer: The LED should light. If it doesn't: check polarity first, then check that row 5 and row 10 really are separate nets.

bigIdea.explorer: Electricity goes in a circle. If the circle is broken, nothing happens.
bigIdea.builder: Electricity only flows in a complete loop, and it always needs a brake - a resistor - or delicate parts burn out.
bigIdea.engineer: Current is the same everywhere in a series loop. The resistor, not the LED, is what sets that current.

goFurther.builder: Swap in the green LED. Is it brighter or dimmer than the red one?
goFurther.engineer: Swap to the green LED. Its higher Vf means less voltage across the resistor, so less current. Predict the change, then check it.

goFurther.explorer: Try the bigger brake. Is it dimmer?
goFurther.builder: Swap the 330Ω for the 1kΩ resistor. What happens to the brightness?
goFurther.engineer: Swap to 1kΩ. Current drops to about 7mA. Is the brightness drop proportional? (It isn't - your eye is logarithmic.)
